title: Time course of visual attention in rats by atomic magnetometer
content:
by Fan Liu, Zhao Xiang, Yuhai Chen, Guanzhong Lu, Jiahao Wang, Jia Yao, Ying Zhang, Xuejiao Ma, Qiang Lin, Yi Ruan

Atomic magnetometer (AM) is utilized to non-invasively detect event-related magnetic fields (ERMFs) evoked by visual stimuli in rats. The aim of this study was to investigate the relationship between N2-like amplitude and visual attention. To achieve this, we combined the AM with a visual stimulation system and employed the passive single-stimulus paradigm. By measuring the ERMFs at various inter-stimulus intervals (ISIs) with a sensitivity of 20 fT/Hz, we analyzed the effects of the ISI and the ‘habituation’ resulting from repeated stimuli on the N2-like amplitude. Our method serves as a valuable reference for studying the passive single-stimulus paradigm and the time course of mammalian attention.
author: Fan Liu
